Account ownership: the representative measure from the Global Findex 2021 wave

01What does this evidence establish?

The latest representative observation of account ownership in Yemen published by the World Bank remains 11.9%. World Bank Data reports it for 2022; it comes from the Yemen Global Findex 2021 study, fielded from 7 November 2022 to 9 January 2023. The Global Findex 2025 edition adds 2024 observations for many economies, but no newer Yemen observation.

01What does this evidence establish?02What does it measure?03Who or what does it apply to?04How current is it?05What this evidence does not establish06Original source and verification07Method and verification detail

02What does it measure?

Account ownership as defined by Global Findex: the share of adults aged 15 and over in the areas the survey covered who report having an account, alone or with someone else, at a bank or another type of financial institution, or who report personally using a mobile-money service in the past 12 months (2021 Findex wave, fieldwork 7 November 2022 to 9 January 2023).

03Who or what does it apply to?

Adults 15+ in survey coverage

04How current is it?

This is the latest observation available for Yemen: World Bank Data reports it for 2022, from the Global Findex 2021 study fielded from 7 November 2022 to 9 January 2023. The Global Findex 2025 edition adds 2024 observations for many economies but no newer observation for Yemen, so the value does not describe 2024, 2025 or 2026.

05What this evidence does not establish

It is not a 2026 rate, and it cannot be broken down or mapped by governorate. It is not the share of adults with a bank account: accounts at other financial institutions and personal use of a mobile-money service also count.

Limits of the measure

The survey frame excludes areas holding about 23% of the population, and more than a quarter of primary sampling units were replaced.
